newsitem.title: UK: Gilts at head of government debt league - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Gilts at head of government debt league - Salomon.

text.p: British gilts shot to the top of the league of major government bonds this week, leaving high yielders Spain and Italy trailing far behind, data from Salomon Brothers showed on Friday.
Bond performance was middling in the week ended on Thursday, with Salomon's World Government Bond Index up 0.47 percent.

Gilts achieved 1.42 percent returns in sterling in the week and an even more impressive 2.51 percent in dollar terms. The market gained after the Bank of England made it clear on Thursday it was not increasing interest rates for now.
Canada was not far behind Britain, scoring 1.19 percent returns, while U.S. Treasuries came in third at 0.66 percent.

All markets spent the week in a state of apprehension over U.S. employment data due on Friday. A Reuter poll showed the consensus was for a rise in average hourly earnings, which would provide evidence of mounting inflationary pressure.
Germany and Austria were up 0.43 and 0.45 percent respectively.
Sweden also managed gains of 0.43 percent, but fellow high yielders Spain and Italy dipped into negative terrority, each posting losses of 0.04 percent.
While they were the only two yielding negative returns in local currencies, results were worse in dollar terms as the greenback charged ahead against many currencies.
Only three out of the 16 countries listed ended up in positive territory -- Britain, Canada and Switzerland.

France came in at the lower end of the list, posting returns of 0.36 percent in francs and minus 0.29 in dollars. Japan, meanwhile, was barely changed from the previous week in yen terms, with gains of 0.03. However, the burgeoning dollar took its toll, knocking dollar JGB returns back 1.43 percent.
